# Spec: spend-cap-opt-in
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-07 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-19 (requested by the owner, 2026-11-07) -->

## Overview
The launcher's spend limits become opt-in. Today `hooks/session-launch.sh:194` reads
`orchestrate.usd_cap // 20` and `orchestrate.daily_usd_cap // 100`, so a project that sets no cap is
silently capped at 20 USD per session and 100 USD per day. After this change a project with no cap
configured launches with no `--max-budget-usd` and no daily refusal; a project that sets a value keeps
exactly today's behaviour. This amends `session-orchestration` FR-011 (session cap) and FR-013 (daily cap)
only in their defaults.

## Decisions (made from the code, recorded so the reviewer can check them)
- **D1 — each cap is independent.** "Opt-in" applies to each key on its own: `usd_cap` governs
  `--max-budget-usd`; `daily_usd_cap` governs the daily refusal. The item's phrase "a missing or null
  `usd_cap` means … no daily check" is read together with "no per-session or daily limit **unless the project
  sets one**": a project that sets `daily_usd_cap` has set a limit, and silently ignoring it because
  `usd_cap` is absent would break that sentence. So:
  - neither set → no flag, no daily check;
  - only `usd_cap` set → the flag, no daily check;
  - both set → today's rule (`spent today + usd_cap > daily_usd_cap` refuses);
  - only `daily_usd_cap` set → no flag; the next session's cost is unknown, so it counts as 0 and the launch
    is refused when **spent today ≥ daily_usd_cap** (`≥`, not `>`: a board already at its limit must not
    start an unbounded session).
- **D2 — "unset" means missing, `null` (or `false`, which jq's `//` treats alike).** Any other value is
  passed through as today (`0` stays `0`: `--max-budget-usd 0` and an always-hit daily cap of 0 are the
  project's explicit choice). Validating non-numeric values is out of scope (unchanged behaviour).
- **D3 — written defaults become open.** `status-board.sh --init` (`hooks/board-setup.sh` `board_init`) and
  the config examples in the guides no longer write `usd_cap: 20, daily_usd_cap: 100`; caps are shown as an
  optional key the project may add. Existing configs that already carry values are not touched.
- **D1 is a named deviation** from the item's literal sentence ("a missing or null `usd_cap` means … no daily
  check"): with `usd_cap` unset but `daily_usd_cap` set, the daily check still runs. The PR description says so
  in one line, so the owner can reverse it (drop the daily-only branch) cheaply.
- **D5 — no "uncapped" notice.** The launcher prints nothing extra when both caps are unset: the item asks
  for the default to be open, not announced, and the CHANGELOG entry at release names the change.
  `hefesto-sdlc.html:813` shows an example (5/25), not a default, and is left as is.
- **D4 — evals and the 9.2.0 launch fixture are unchanged.** Every `evals/*/scaffold.sh` and
  `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt` set explicit caps (5/25 etc.), so their behaviour is today's by FR-002.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A project with no cap launches uncapped [P1]
- **Given** `.claude/project-status.json` has no `orchestrate.usd_cap` and no `orchestrate.daily_usd_cap`
  (no `orchestrate` block at all, or the keys set to `null`)
- **When** `session-launch.sh implement <id> --dry-run` prints the command line
- **Then** the line carries no `--max-budget-usd` token, and every other flag is as before
- **Edge:** `"usd_cap": null` explicitly → same as missing
- **Error / must NOT:** a launch is never refused with "daily cap … would be exceeded" whatever today's spend is

### US2: A set cap keeps today's behaviour [P1]
- **Given** `orchestrate.usd_cap: 5` and `orchestrate.daily_usd_cap: 8`, with 3.45 USD spent today
- **When** an implement run is launched
- **Then** it is refused before any claim, naming the daily cap (today's rule)
- **Edge:** `usd_cap: 5` with `daily_usd_cap: 100` → the line carries `--max-budget-usd 5` and the run goes ahead
- **Error:** a session that stops with result subtype `error_max_budget_usd` is still a `budget` block

### US3: Only a daily cap is set [P2]
- **Given** `daily_usd_cap: 2` and no `usd_cap`
- **When** a launch happens with 2 USD or more spent today
- **Then** it is refused before any claim with a message naming the daily cap and today's spend, without
  "session cap" arithmetic on an empty value
- **Edge:** with 1.5 USD spent → the launch proceeds, no `--max-budget-usd` on the line
- **Must NOT:** the deploy stage's merge record (launches nothing) is refused — it still passes over the cap

### US4: New boards and the guides say "open by default" [P2]
- **Given** a fresh repository
- **When** `status-board.sh --init` writes `.claude/project-status.json`
- **Then** its `orchestrate` block has no `usd_cap` and no `daily_usd_cap` key (the other defaults —
  `plan_review`, `plan_first`, `rfc_dir` — are unchanged)
- **And** `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`,
  `README.md` and `SETUP.md` describe both caps as opt-in with no default, and no longer state "$20 by
  default" / "$100" as the default

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | With `orchestrate.usd_cap` missing or null, the launched command line carries no `--max-budget-usd` flag (`hooks/session-launch.sh`) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | With `orchestrate.usd_cap` set, `--max-budget-usd <value>` is on the line exactly as today; with both caps set the daily refusal is today's `spent + usd_cap > daily_usd_cap` rule, before any claim | P1 | US2 |
| FR-003 | With `orchestrate.daily_usd_cap` missing or null, no daily-cap refusal happens on any role or path (both the pre-claim check and the deploy stage's babysit check) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | With only `daily_usd_cap` set, a launch is refused before any claim when today's spend ≥ the daily cap; the message names the daily cap and today's spend | P2 | US3 |
| FR-005 | The deploy stage's merge record still passes over a hit daily cap (it launches nothing); babysitting still refuses | P2 | US3 |
| FR-006 | `status-board.sh --init` writes an `orchestrate` block with no `usd_cap` / `daily_usd_cap` keys; its other keys are unchanged | P2 | US4 |
| FR-007 | The orchestrate guide (`commands/hef.orchestrate.md`), `docs/install.md`, `docs/hooks.md` (the `session-launch.sh` row, "$20 a run and $100 a day"), `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`, `README.md` and `SETUP.md` describe the caps as opt-in, open by default; the orchestrator's "Spend today" line reports spend with no cap when none is set | P2 | US4 |
| FR-008 | `tests/smoke.sh` covers: the no-cap dry-run (no flag), the null-cap dry-run, the set-cap dry-run (flag), the daily refusal with both caps, the daily-only refusal, no refusal with no daily cap even when spend is high, the budget block, and the init defaults — each with a mutation that turns it red | P1 | US1–US4 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | `bash tests/smoke.sh` passes, including the rewritten default-cap assertion (`tests/smoke.sh:1993` now asserts the flag's absence) | run the suite |
| SC-002 | Every test added for FR-001..FR-006 fails when its guarded line is reverted to the `// 20` / `// 100` defaults | the mutation embedded next to each test |
| SC-003 | No file in `hooks/`, `commands/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `SETUP.md` states 20/100 USD as a default cap | `grep -rnE '\$ ?20 (a run|by default)|\$ ?100 a day|usd_cap.{0,4}// (20|100)|US\$ 20 por padrão|usd_cap: 20, daily_usd_cap: 100|"usd_cap": ?20|"daily_usd_cap": ?100'` over those paths returns nothing — and, run on the tree before the change, hits all seven doc files plus `hooks/session-launch.sh:194` and `hooks/board-setup.sh:41` (so the check can fail) |
| SC-004 | `tests/smoke-spec-roots.sh` still equals `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt` (its fixture sets explicit caps) | run that suite |
